title: Canonical relative higher-image diagram and cocone laws
statement: Let I be a preorder, DV and DB inverse systems of schemes, and η:DV→DB a natural transformation. Let cV,cB be cones and v:cV.pt→cB.pt commute with their stage maps. Give sheaves F_i on DV_i, coherent inverse-image coefficient maps φ, and a diagram A on cV.pt with object isomorphisms eA_i:A_i≅p_i⁻¹F_i whose transitions are the prescribed pullbacks of φ. Let cA be any cocone of A and q a natural number. Write G_i=R^qη_i,* F_i, O_i=s_i⁻¹G_i, and define M_ij by the inverse-image composition isomorphism for s_i=b_ij s_j followed by pullback of the commutative-square exchange with coefficient φ_ij. Define L_i:O_i→R^qv_*cA.pt by projection exchange followed by the coefficient leg (eA_i)⁻¹ then cA.ι_i. Then M_id=id, M_ik=M_ij M_jk, and M_ij L_j=L_i. No cartesian, affine, qcqs, directedness, torsion or universal cone hypothesis is assumed. The data use [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-kun-commutative-derived-exchange], and [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

proof.text: Paste consecutive transition squares horizontally. Apply the derived exchange horizontal composition identity, then naturality for the coefficient map, and the coefficient composition equation. Apply degree-q homology. Exact inverse image commutes with homology, and the composition and single-functor comparisons give the displayed transitions. Inverse-image associativity identifies the two routes from a limiting projection to the composite transition. Hence M(a≫b)=M(a)≫M(b).

The derived identity-square exchange is an isomorphism by the identity pasting formula. The coefficient identity equation makes its coefficient map an isomorphism. Thus M(id) is an isomorphism. The composition equation gives M(id)=M(id)≫M(id); cancel M(id) to obtain the identity law.

Paste a transition square with the projection square at its target. The horizontal composition formula and coefficient naturality rewrite M(a)≫L(j) as the projection exchange at i followed by the higher image of the composite coefficient leg. The equation for A.map a and the cocone relation for cA identify that coefficient leg with (eA i).inv≫cA.ι.app i. Thus M(a)≫L(j)=L(i).

lean.statement:
theorem relativeHigherImage_cone_laws
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I]
    (DV DB : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (η : DV ⟶ DB)
    (cV : Cone DV) (cB : Cone DB) (v : cV.pt ⟶ cB.pt)
    (hu : ∀ i, cV.π.app i ≫ η.app i = v ≫ cB.π.app i)
    (F : ∀ i : I, Sheaf (DV.obj (op i)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (φ : ∀ {i j : I} (a : i ⟶ j),
      ((DV.map a.op)^*[AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}]).obj (F i) ⟶ F j)
    (hid : ∀ i, φ (𝟙 i) =
      eqToHom (congrArg (fun a : DV.obj (op i) ⟶ DV.obj (op i) ↦
        ((a)^*[AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}]).obj (F i)) (DV.map_id (op i))) ≫
        (upperStarId AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (DV.obj (op i))).hom.app (F i))
    (hcomp : ∀ (i j k : I) (a : i ⟶ j) (b : j ⟶ k), φ (a ≫ b) =
      (upperStarComp AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (DV.map b.op) (DV.map a.op)
        (DV.map (a ≫ b).op) (DV.map_comp b.op a.op)).hom.app (F i) ≫
      ((DV.map b.op)^*[AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}]).map (φ a) ≫ φ b)
    (A : I ⥤ Sheaf cV.pt.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (eA : ∀ i, A.obj i ≅ ((cV.π.app (op i))^*[AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}]).obj (F i))
    (hA : ∀ (i j : I) (a : i ⟶ j), A.map a ≫ (eA j).hom =
      (eA i).hom ≫
        (upperStarComp AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (cV.π.app (op j)) (DV.map a.op)
          (cV.π.app (op i)) (cV.w a.op).symm).hom.app (F i) ≫
        ((cV.π.app (op j))^*[AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}]).map (φ a))
    (cA : Cocone A) (q : ℕ) :
    DiagramCoconeLaws (relativeHigherImageObj DV DB η cB F q)
      (relativeHigherImageMap DV DB η cB F φ q) ((higherImageFunctor v q).obj cA.pt)
      (relativeHigherImageLeg DV DB η cV cB v hu F A eA cA q)
